recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes a narrow, traceable part of the published FHIR-16886 decision while preserving the already-applied Binary contentType restructuring.
issue_request: FHIR-16886 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 Binary issue asking to restructure contentType handling guidance for retrieval, create/update, _summary behavior, generic MIME handling, and header mappings, and to address inconsistent lower-case should usage.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14354, represented by git commit 4c0d34042c3e8742eda89fdb336da09c622aa009, together with FHIR-13507. That commit restructured source/binary/binary-notes.xml into the current list form and moved the relevant _summary and create/update guidance, but retained the lower-case should in the non-FHIR Accept-header return rule.
additional_context: Binary is active in the current build and part of the infrastructure normative package. Later Binary edits and reconciliations preserved the same return rule. FHIR-I minutes for 2018-07-09 record FHIR-16886 as Persuasive with Mod, and no direct Zulip or conflicting Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: Changed the active Binary REST narrative so the non-FHIR Accept-header return rule uses uppercase SHOULD, and rephrased the PDF example to avoid a second lower-case conformance-looking should. No other Binary behavior was changed.
source_changes: source/binary/binary-notes.xml: updated the non-FHIR Accept-header return rule from lower-case should to uppercase SHOULD and rephrased the PDF example to avoid duplicate lower-case conformance wording.
